teacher_evidence_manifest.rule: public-context witnesses, then actual rejected-candidate harm, then parent failures; ties by source ID

by_task.when: ARIZONA is allowable and the asset fits an Arizona category.
by_task.procedure: Treat statutory dollar limits as caps, not eligibility thresholds: include § 33-1125(8) for a motor vehicle and § 33-1125(10) for a firearm even when value exceeds the limit. Include § 33-1101(A), not subsection (B), as the homestead exemption alternative. Confirm the statutory category before applying its cap. Section 33-1123 is limited to household furniture, furnishings, household goods, consumer electronic devices, and appliances; do not use it for wearing apparel, jewelry, or musical instruments.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not classify jewelry as wearing apparel; § 33-1125(4) is limited to engagement and wedding rings, and subsection (B) is a one-homestead limitation rather than a separate asset exemption. Non-ring jewelry does not qualify under either § 33-1125(1) or § 33-1125(4).

operations.rationale: Current sources 230 and 239 show false Arizona claims for non-ring jewelry, including misuse of § 33-1123 and § 33-1125(4), while source 230 also shows § 33-1123 incorrectly added to apparel. Historical sources 182 and 223 confirm the same category-boundary problem. Extending the existing boundary to EV and expressly limiting § 33-1123 addresses those false positives without changing the correct vehicle, firearm, homestead, ring, or cap rules.
